name: Ortelian
tagline: A curated mapping product: somebody else's structured judgment about a domain, packaged as software you can browse.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Public detail on this one is thin, so treat the confidence rating as real and not decorative. What is visible is the shape of a curation product: the software is a viewer, and the value is the corpus plus the taste that decided what goes in it and how it connects. A coding agent can rebuild the viewer in a weekend, including search, tagging, a graph view and clean exports, and it will look fine and be empty. Filling it is not a coding problem, it is months of reading, deciding and re-deciding, which is the part you were paying someone else to have already done. Build the shell if you want your own private map of a domain you already know deeply; do not build it expecting to get the map itself.
coreLoopDIY: A local app where you write structured entries in markdown, link them to each other, and browse the result as a searchable list plus an interactive graph.
requirements: Your own corpus: every entry is on you
Ongoing time to maintain it, or it rots in a month
whatYouLose: The actual content, which is the whole product
Someone else's editorial judgment about what matters and what is noise
Updates when the underlying domain shifts
Consistent structure across hundreds of entries, which is boring, expensive work
Polish: a hand-built graph view is usable, not pleasant
moatNotes: Curation moats look soft until you try to reproduce one. The schema is copyable in an afternoon, the entries are not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is doing the reading yourself. People buy curated maps of a domain for the same reason they buy a good textbook instead of forty tabs: someone competent already sorted the signal, chose a structure, and kept it current. The software around it is close to irrelevant to that decision, which is exactly why rebuilding the software does not get you out of paying.
notes: Rendering a map is a weekend; deciding what belongs on it is the product. The moat is the accumulated corpus and the judgment calls baked into its structure, not the viewer wrapped around them.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal knowledge map app in an empty folder. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20, TypeScript, Vite + React for the UI
- Fastify for a tiny local API on port 5173/3001
- Content stored as markdown files with YAML frontmatter in ./content, one file per entry
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 as a derived index only, rebuilt from ./content on startup and on file change (chokidar)
- Cytoscape.js for the graph view

Data model: each entry has id (slug from filename), title, kind (concept | source | person | org | question), tags[], summary (one paragraph), body (markdown), links[] (array of { to: entryId, relation: string }). Validate frontmatter with zod and print clear errors for bad files instead of crashing.

Features in scope:
- Left pane: full-text search over title, summary, body using SQLite FTS5, plus filters by kind and tag
- Center: entry reader rendering markdown, with inbound and outbound links listed and labeled by relation
- Right: local graph of the current entry, 1 and 2 hops, click a node to navigate
- Full graph page, colored by kind, with tag filter
- "Orphans and stubs" report: entries with no links, or summary under 20 words
- Export: one JSON file of all entries and links, and a static HTML build of the reader
- Seed ./content with 6 example entries showing every field and relation type

Explicitly out of scope: auth, multi-user, sync, any hosted service, AI generation of entries, scraping. If you want an optional local LLM summarizer, put it behind an env flag defaulting to off and read the key from .env, which must be gitignored.

Include a README stating plainly that this ships empty and that the content is the actual work. Add npm scripts: dev, build, reindex, export.
